headline: A short-term spending bill keeps most federal agencies funded through May 5, 2017, and extends health benefits for certain retired coal miners.
what_it_does: The resolution continues federal funding for most agencies at current levels until the earlier of May 5, 2017, or when full spending bills for fiscal year 2017 are enacted. Without it, funding would lapse after April 28, 2017, because 11 of the 12 regular spending bills for the year had not passed. It also extends, through May 5, 2017, a provision that pays health care benefits for certain retired miners and their families.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agency employees and federal contractors
who_it_affects.how: Their agencies keep operating without a funding gap, so paychecks and contract work can continue on schedule.

who_it_affects.group: Certain retired coal miners and their families
who_it_affects.how: Their health care benefits under a provision of the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act are extended through May 5, 2017.

who_it_affects.group: People who use federal government services
who_it_affects.how: Most federal offices and programs stay open instead of facing a partial shutdown after April 28, 2017.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted April 28, 2017; funding runs through May 5, 2017, or until full fiscal year 2017 appropriations are enacted, whichever comes first.
